::: {.why}
Cost is a rate and turnover is the quantity it multiplies, which means every conversation about whether a strategy survives costs is really a conversation about turnover.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Express net Sharpe as a function of gross Sharpe, turnover and cost per unit traded, and check the algebra against your engine.
- Report the turnover at which each of your strategies breaks even.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Derive the relationship: annual cost equals one-way turnover times round-trip cost, and net return is gross return minus that. Write net Sharpe in terms of the three quantities, then verify the formula reproduces your engine's net number to within rounding for both strategies.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Find the levers: for each strategy, compute how much gross Sharpe you would need at twice the turnover to hold net Sharpe constant, and how much turnover you could cut by halving the rebalance frequency, with the resulting loss in signal freshness. This trade-off is what phase 6 optimises rather than the raw signal.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Add turnover reporting to the result object so every strategy carries it without being asked.
:::
:::

:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
A strategy has a Sharpe of 2.0 before costs and 0.3 after. What is its turnover, roughly, and what would you change first?
:::
